title: Future Continuous
subtitle: Say what will already be in progress at a specific future moment.
objectives: Use it for an action in progress at a specific future time
Use it to ask politely about someone's plans

content.intro: Imagine pointing to a moment on the calendar next week and asking "what will be happening then?" That's exactly what the future continuous describes.

rules.heading: Use 1: in progress at a specific future time
rules.body:
• This time tomorrow, I will be flying to New York.
  • At 8pm, we will be having dinner.

rules.heading: Use 2: polite questions about plans
rules.body: • Will you be using the car tonight? (asking without sounding demanding)

examples: This time tomorrow, I will be flying to New York.
At 8pm, we will be having dinner.
She will be working late tonight.
Will you be coming to the meeting?
They will be traveling all week.
By this time next year, he will be living abroad.

commonMistakes.wrong: This time tomorrow, I will flying to New York.
commonMistakes.right: This time tomorrow, I will be flying to New York.
commonMistakes.why: The future continuous needs "be" before the -ing verb.

commonMistakes.wrong: She will be work late tonight.
commonMistakes.right: She will be working late tonight.
commonMistakes.why: After "will be," the verb needs the -ing form, not the base form.

commonMistakes.right: At 8pm, we will be having dinner.
commonMistakes.why: "Will" and the -ing form always need "be" between them.

items.prompt: This time tomorrow, I ___ (fly) to New York.
By this time next year, he ___ abroad.
items.explanation: An action in progress at a specific future point — future continuous.
Question form: Will + subject + be + -ing ("Will" comes first, before the subject).

answer: They will be traveling all week.
items.explanation: The future continuous needs "be" before the -ing form.

items.incorrect: She will be work late tonight.
answer: She will be working late tonight.
items.explanation: After "will be," use the -ing form, not the base form.

summary: Will be + verb-ing, the same for every subject.
Use it for an action already in progress at a specific future moment.
Also useful for polite questions about someone's plans.
